assumptions: There are enough smaller responsible operators not already committed to an ERP, certifier, or DPP platform.
Their upstream suppliers can provide authentic required fields on a workable timetable.
A service provider can integrate with the registry and process records under narrowly scoped customer authority.
A customer-hosted or portable architecture can contain long-lived availability and migration liability.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots from several unrelated operators showing actual missing-field patterns, supplier response rates, onboarding hours, registry acceptance, annual support burden, gross margin, portability, and a signed repeatable channel agreement.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The 71-field passport requirement turns scattered supplier evidence into a concrete model-onboarding and maintained unit-record workflow for smaller responsible operators.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: A hard market-access date and clearly responsible economic operator create urgent accountable pain, although willingness to outsource and the actual labor or delay cost remain unproven.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Model onboarding plus annual or unit hosting offers setup and recurring revenue, but supplier exception labor, security, registry work, support, durable availability, and migration reserves are not costed from experience.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Smaller importers and assemblers facing the 2027 deadline are a plausible underserved beachhead, though the proposal still spans several battery categories and lacks a counted regional target list.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Battery-specific onboarding for smaller operators may beat generic suites on service, but DPP vendors, ERP providers, certifiers, battery firms, and consultancies can readily bundle the required workflow.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Once proven, supplier-evidence mappings and passport operations can extend across battery categories, countries, lifecycle updates, and eventually adjacent DPP-regulated products.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Field-level defect patterns and supplier mappings can reduce later onboarding effort, but customer data cannot be reused beyond the service and customers retain the legal duty and underlying information.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The founder's data-lineage skills and sector interest fit the work, but no battery customer, supplier right, registry authorization, channel agreement, or operating dataset is controlled.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The registry is operational, detailed Commission guidance is available, and the February 2027 mandatory date creates a short, unusually strong readiness window.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Testing labs, certifiers, import advisers, distributors, ERP partners, and associations are well aligned with the trigger, but no referral or integration route is contracted.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A readiness service and one-model prototype are feasible, but incomplete supplier data, security, integrity, registry details, hosting longevity, and migration liability can make delivery service-heavy.

highest_value_structural_change: Narrow to one battery category and sell a customer-hosted supplier-completeness and validation layer through a signed certifier or import-adviser channel, leaving durable passport hosting and legal responsibility with the operator.
main_structural_strength: A mandatory near-term market-access requirement identifies the responsible payer and creates repeat paid events at model onboarding, unit issuance, and lifecycle update.
primary_score_limiter: No operator data right or channel is secured, and incomplete supplier inputs plus entrenched DPP and ERP vendors can prevent delivery or compress the venture into low-margin implementation work.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The DPP and standards ecosystem is already operating, favoring established platforms, while legal responsibility remains with the economic operator and service providers cannot monetize passport data beyond the necessary service.
